messages:
Alex (Support): forwarding a customer escalation — embeddings endpoint failing for batched requests. Customer says single-item calls succeed but batch calls return a dimension mismatch error and sometimes time out. Error snippets below. filing ticket INF-8421 and attaching logs.

Customer error: 
```
HTTP 400 Bad Request
{
  "error": "dimension_mismatch",
  "message": "expected vector dim=1536 got 1024 for item 2"
}
```

Repro steps the customer gave:
1) Using Python SDK v0.9.1, send a batch of 8 texts to /v1/embeddings with model "open-embed-1536"
2) Some items return 1536-d vectors, some 1024-d.
3) Go client gets context deadline exceeded on the same payload when retried.
4) TS client (browser) sees partial successes, then 400.

Alex: initial guesses — could be a model variant fallback (1536 vs 1024), or a batching/packing bug where the server re-uses a different model shard. Also possible SDK is passing wrong model name for some items in batch.

Maria (Eng-ML): can you paste the raw request body (redact PII)? if the batch encoding mixes models that would explain mixed dims. Also, are these requests hitting dedicated or hosted?

Alex (Support): customer on hosted API (eu-west). Raw payload (redacted):
```
POST /v1/embeddings
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "model": "open-embed-1536",
  "input": ["doc a", "doc b", "doc c", "doc d", "doc e", "doc f", "doc g", "doc h"]
}
```

Sam (Eng-Runtime): quick check — we recently added an optimization that batches multiple small requests into a single runtime batch and may route different queued batches to different compiled kernels. If one kernel is for a 1024-d variant (legacy quantized) due to model alias resolution, that would produce mixed dims. We should look at routing logs for that timespan.

Jin (DevEx): flagging a possible Python SDK packing bug: earlier SDK versions accidentally convert list-of-strings to a single newline-joined string when serializing under certain conditions leading to per-item model fallback. Also saw an issue where header "X-Client-Model" gets stripped by HTTP proxies, forcing server fallback. Customer is on Python v0.9.1 which matches a reported issue.

Alex: customer also included a trace showing different vector lengths per item: first 3 are 1536, items 4-6 are 1024, items 7-8 timed out.

Lee (SRE): ops-bot shows increased 5xx and 400s on embeddings in eu-west around that window. Pushing routing logs to the thread: ops-bot: /logs/embeddings/eu-west/1765001200-1765001300 (internal link).

ops-bot: Incident alert: embeddings-eu-west high-error-rate (ID: 2026-03-12-emb-eu).

Maria (Eng-ML): probable chain: client serializes batch incorrectly -> server applies model alias resolution on per-item basis (fallback to 1024 variant for malformed items) -> mixed dims -> client sees 400. Timeouts likely from retry storms because SDKs retry each item on top of batch retries.

Sam (Eng-Runtime): to triage: can we reproduce locally with the exact Python payload and SDK version? Also capture the raw HTTP/2 frames to verify the body splitting. I'll add a debug flag to the runtime to log per-item resolved model id.

Jin (DevEx): repro test I ran locally: Python SDK v0.9.1 produced this when input list had a stray None (customer sanitized but may have empty strings). Minimal repro: 
```
from redwood import EmbeddingsClient
client = EmbeddingsClient(api_key=...)
texts = ["a","b","","d"]  # empty string present
resp = client.embeddings(model="open-embed-1536", input=texts, timeout=5)
```
Result: server accepted, but the third item returned 1024 dims.

Maria: empty string shouldn't cause fallback but we do have an alias map: open-embed-1536 -> [open-embed-1536-v1, open-embed-1024-compat] for older shards. If input is encoded as an empty payload maybe the allocator picks the compat shard.

Alex: customer also reported Go SDK timeouts. Any known issues?

Jin (DevEx): Go SDK had a default client timeout of 2s for embeddings batch calls in v0.8.x — that's too low for larger batches. Recommend bumping to 15s and enabling exponential backoff with jitter. Example patch for Go: 
```go
client, _ := redwood.NewClient(opts...)
client.Timeout = 15 * time.Second
client.RetryPolicy = redwood.ExponentialBackoff(3, 200*time.Millisecond)
```

Sam: runtime note — batching large inputs can push request processing >2s depending on GPU queue. We run a token-cost/latency estimator; for eu-west at that time the average batch latency was 1.8s but p99 4.2s. So Go default 2s will see failures.

Alex: immediate customer-facing steps to resolve:
- Ask customer to try single-item calls (they already did — worked).
- Patch Python SDK to v0.9.2 (contains fix for list serialization bug) and retry the same batch.
- Increase client timeout on Go and TS clients.
- If issue persists, capture raw POST body and share with us + request ID header (X-Request-ID).

Maria: longer-term fixes: disallow cross-model resolution inside a single batch (atomic model resolution), add server validation to reject batches where resolved vector dims vary, and add clearer 4xx error message referencing item index. Creating follow-up RFC RFC-emb-batch-atomic.

Sam: operational mitigation: add runtime check to reject mixed-dim responses and log offending request IDs with full resolved model list. Rolling a small telemetry patch to prod in canary for 30 minutes.

Jin: draft of customer reply (short):
"Thanks — we think this was caused by a serialization edge case in Python SDK v0.9.1 leading to per-item model fallback. Please try v0.9.2; for Go/TS increase timeouts and enable retries. If you still see dimension_mismatch, send the raw POST body and X-Request-ID and we'll correlate with our routing logs." :thumbsup:

Alex: customer tried v0.9.2 and confirmed batch now returns consistent 1536 dims for their test set. They also increased Go timeout and retried — no more timeouts. Customer happy, closing the ticket after 24h observation window.

Maria: follow-ups — RFC + runtime guard tracked in INF-8421 and ENG-ML backlog.

Sam: I'll keep the canary telemetry on for 2h.

Lee: ops-bot: incident resolved, error-rate back to normal. :white_check_mark:

Alex: marking for postmortem writeup: short blameless summary, root cause (SDK serialization bug + permissive runtime aliasing), mitigations (SDK patch, server validation), customer impact, timeline. Assigning to Maria/Sam/Jin.

Jin: I'll add a short bullet in the SDK changelog.

Alex: thanks all. :slightly_smiling_face:
